title: Forty-eight ways (Avot 6:6)
hook: Torah is acquired by a listening ear, ordered speech, an understanding heart, and forty-five more
tomorrow: you repeat a friend's great line. whose line is it now?

segments.voice: Yesterday, bread with salt: the bare minimum, and the learning starts right there. So if it isn't things, what does it take?
screen: `BREAD WITH SALT.` → `SO WHAT DOES IT TAKE?`

segments.voice: A job posting lists forty-eight requirements, and most of us would close the tab. Avot 6:6 has a list like that, and it opens with a comparison. Kingship is acquired with thirty qualities. Priesthood with twenty-four. Torah with forty-eight. It reads almost like a scoreboard, and the book wins by a lot. That's the odd detail. Why would a book of teaching take more to get than a throne?
screen: `FORTY-EIGHT REQUIREMENTS.` → `A CROWN TAKES THIRTY.` → `WHY DOES TORAH TAKE MORE?`

segments.voice: Start with how a king and a priest got the job in the Bible. David's line held the crown. Aaron's sons held the priesthood. You were born into them, or you weren't. Now read the forty-eight. The list opens: with study, with a listening ear, with ordered speech, with an understanding heart. Further down: with humility, with joy, with serving the sages, with the give-and-take of friends and students, loving rebuke, being happy with your portion. None of them comes with a family name. Each one is something a person does, or slowly becomes. That's the puzzle solved. A crown is handed down. Torah, in this list, can only be acquired, so the list is long, and the door is open. Now notice what sits near the very top, second only to study: a listening ear. In Hebrew, shmi'at ha-ozen, the hearing of the ear. Before ordered speech, before an understanding heart, the list asks you to hear. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: in Avot, a throne takes thirty qualities and Torah takes forty-eight, and not one of the forty-eight needs the right parents. The student in the back row who never gets called on can start with number two.
screen: `A CROWN IS BORN INTO.` · `FORTY-EIGHT THINGS YOU DO.` · `THE DOOR IS OPEN.` · `SECOND ON THE LIST: LISTEN.` · then, large: `A LISTENING EAR.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes if you like, and listen. Find the farthest sound you can hear, then the nearest, then the quietest one in between. Don't name them or judge them; just receive each one, the way the list asks an ear to. If someone nearby is talking, let their voice be one of the sounds, and hear the words without answering them.
Forty-eight ways. Avot's list of how Torah is acquired: more than a crown's thirty, and every one open to anyone.
Pocket this one: a listening ear, second on the list and open to anyone. One day of Avot left.

screen: `DAY 1486 COUNTS.` → `AVOT, CHAPTERS 3–6 · 59 OF 60.` → `TOMORROW: YOU REPEAT A FRIEND'S GREAT LINE. WHOSE IS IT NOW?`

howItsDone: In a yeshiva or a study group, much of learning happens out loud in pairs, so listening to a partner's reading is part of the work; many people also study Avot's sixth chapter, with its forty-eight ways, on Shabbat afternoons.

fork.setup: a group meeting where everyone talks over each other and nothing gets decided. you have a strong idea. which of the forty-eight comes first?
options: a listening ear: hear what's been said before adding yours.
ordered speech: say your idea clearly enough to win the room.
happy with your portion: let the others decide and stay out of it.
fork.reveal: all three are on the list, but the listening ear comes before ordered speech. hearing first is the step most of us skip.

original.note: Hebrew: the hearing of the ear, a listening ear, second of Avot's forty-eight ways.

trapdoor: what you thought: a long checklist for scholars.
what it means: Torah is acquired, never inherited, through forty-eight things anyone can do, starting with study and a listening ear.
what a scholar hears: the list measures itself against kingship (thirty) and priesthood (twenty-four), two offices held by family line in the Bible.

chat.meaning: Among the forty-eight ways to acquire Torah, a listening ear comes second, before speaking well. Hearing it again, really hearing, counts.

Avot.meaning: Pirkei Avot, the Mishnah's book of sages' sayings

Torah.meaning: God's teaching; the five books of Moses, and learning itself

shmi'at ha-ozen.meaning: the hearing of the ear: a listening ear

Aaron.meaning: Moses' brother, the first high priest, whose sons held the priesthood

sources.ref: Mishnah Avot 6:6 (Torah is greater than priesthood and kingship: thirty, twenty-four, forty-eight; the list of the forty-eight)
Numbers 18:1–7; 2 Samuel 7:12–16 (priesthood to Aaron's sons; the kingdom to David's line)
